r.method: For every candidate: zoomed render.py windows (3x3 to 5x5 m, 0.25 m grid, a/b marks, inserts) plus 5-10 m context renders per cluster and whole-floor overviews; listed the flattened wall-layer geometry around both ends (prims.load items: LINE / LWPOLYLINE on WALL, COL, D-JAMB, WIN, A-1.Netcat, A-WALL*) to read wall ends, caps, thickness, what is drawn inside the gap and what the wall does beyond; checked the layer of anything drawn in gaps (single WALL-layer lines, TREE / X lines, Netthay-manh thin lines, Defpoints room polygons, furniture). Rule used: real-passage = two free ends / corners / piers of the same wall line face each other, the wall carries on beyond both, nothing wall-like is drawn across; mouth = a wall end / corner / pier faces the side of a perpendicular wall (or two wall sides of an aisle or lobby) with no wall line interrupted; not-opening = gap closed by something drawn (single wall-layer line, box, window across a recess, planter X), ends in open space, or the line passes through a wall/door. Result: 7 real-passage (P-03, P-06, P-13, P-16, P-23, P-30, P-33), 18 mouth, 11 not-opening. Low-confidence calls: P-02, P-03, P-08, P-11, P-17, P-20, P-21, P-33. r.method: Judged from the drawing alone with the shared prims cache (no detector output, keys or plan files read). For each of the 36 places: rendered it at 3 m and 7 m with my own renderer (solid wall lines black, columns brown, axis/hidden/dashed wall-layer lines orange dashed so grid axes are not mistaken for walls, door/window/glass/jamb layers coloured, candidate segment drawn with ends a/b); listed the layers, linetypes and block paths of everything around both ends and along the segment; and ran a script that, per end, measures whether a collinear wall continues outward or the end lies on the side/end of a perpendicular wall, and whether any solid wall/door/glass/window line crosses or runs along the segment (only P-20 has a solid wall line along it; all other lines along segments are dashed grid axes or hidden outlines). Rule used: real-passage = both ends are end faces of collinear wall(s) that carry on beyond them, with nothing solid drawn across (doorless doorway/opening); mouth = one end meets the side (or end/pier/corner) of a wall perpendicular to the segment, i.e. a corridor, aisle or room open side seen in section; not-opening = closed or explained by a drawn element (single wall line, window+planter niche, void X symbol), a niche/recess, or a span across a room/door. Lower confidence where the wall pieces may be joinery or exterior structures (P-03, P-08, P-33, P-34) or where a mouth works functionally as a cased doorway (P-26, P-27). Result: 10 real-passage (P-03, P-06, P-07, P-08, P-13, P-16, P-23, P-30, P-33, P-34; high confidence for P-06, P-13, P-16, P-23, P-30), 19 mouth, 7 not-opening.
